result.title: Who Writes the Codebook? An Eight-Step Framework for Auditing LLM-Generated Category Systems
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly create the categories through which qualitative evidence is interpreted. Existing coding benchmarks often hold these categories fixed. We propose the Qualitative Variance Audit Framework, an eight-step method that compares codebook creation, repeated application and code distributions under controlled inputs. It combines model-owned and shared-reference codebooks to distinguish variation in the overall pipeline from application differences within a common category system. An application to 668 organisational interviews, 13,166 text units and eight models from five vendors yields 48 codebooks and 270 coding runs. Models create markedly different category structures; mean within-model reliability ranges from .76 to .92, whereas between-model agreement on the shared codebook is about .69. The framework complements LLM-assisted grounded theory by exposing model dependencies before substantive interpretation. It assesses reliability and representational consequences, not interpretive validity or the quality of resulting theory.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「质性方差审计框架」，用八步流程在受控输入下比较多个模型自建与共享参考码本的类别结构、重复编码的一致性与码分布，并以 668 份访谈、8 个模型的 48 个码本与 270 次编码运行展示模型间类别结构差异远大于模型内可靠性差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把总体管线方差拆成「码本创建」与「同一类别系统内应用」两部分，并报告模型内可靠性与模型间一致性，可能为区分 LVR 中 latent 状态构建与后续使用、以及跨模型 latent 相似度比较提供可核查的测量类比，但领域相距较远。
